description: VECTOR_MIN - every expectation measured on a real Snowflake account. The minimum is ELEMENT-WISE, not row-wise: over [1,9,3], [4,5,-6] and [7,2,0] the answer is [1.000000,2.000000,-6.000000], with each element coming from a DIFFERENT row, so the reduction is per dimension and not 'the smallest row' - same-shaped rows would not have shown this. NULL rows are skipped. Like VECTOR_MAX and unlike VECTOR_AVG it KEEPS the INT element type, which is why the INT case renders [1,5,-6]. An empty or all-NULL group is NULL, a single-row group is that row, and a non-vector argument is a compile error naming the argument's type. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/VectorMinTest (now retired); every vector is read as a bare cell, as recorded in functions-vector-avg.
